THE ANALYTICAL FOUNDATION

What is spatial analysis in GriidAi?

Spatial analysis in GriidAi is the use of explicit GIS operations to answer questions about location, distance, overlap, terrain, raster values, flow, networks, and spatial relationships. The platform connects natural-language intent to supported geospatial tools, prepares an execution plan, lets the user review the method, and then produces spatial outputs that can be inspected on the map or in tables.

The AI layer guides and orchestrates the work, but the analytical result is still grounded in spatial data, coordinate systems, processing operations, parameters, and validation checks rather than a text-only response.

02 / VECTOR ANALYSIS

Analyze spatial relationships between features

GriidAi supports feature-based analysis for questions involving location, distance, overlap, selection, and geometry. Users can work from selected map features or attribute criteria and then apply supported GIS primitives as part of a reviewed analytical sequence.

BUILDING PROXIMITY EXAMPLE

Which buildings are within 50 meters of the selected property?

  1. Select the building to analyze.
  2. Buffer the selected feature by 50 meters after reviewing the plan.
  3. Intersect neighboring buildings with the buffer.
  4. Inspect the selected buildings and resulting map.
See the building proximity walkthrough ↗

Buffer

Create distance-based zones around selected or specified features.

Intersect / overlay

Identify or derive spatial relationships where layers overlap.

Clip / overlay primitives

Use standardized vector processing within supported workflows.

Attribute selection

Select features using attribute conditions and save the selection as a new layer.

Feature selection

Select spatial features directly from the map for analysis.

Field cleanup

Rename supported fields without re-uploading the dataset.

03 / RASTER ANALYSIS

Work with continuous surfaces, imagery, and raster calculations

Raster analysis in GriidAi connects raster datasets with explicit calculations and spatial workflows. Supported operations include raster algebra, zonal statistics, visualization, and raster export. Demonstrated workflows combine elevation-derived analysis with raster and vector processing.

Raster algebra

Use explicit raster calculations as part of a supported analytical sequence.

Zonal statistics

Summarize raster values by zones.

Raster visualization

Inspect raster data in grayscale, multiband, or pseudocolor views where relevant.

Raster and vector together

Use building footprints as zones over a surface raster in the rooftop-solar screening example.

Raster export

Export analytical raster outputs as GeoTIFF.

04 / TERRAIN ANALYSIS

Turn elevation surfaces into terrain information

GriidAi includes terrain-processing capabilities for working with digital elevation data. In the demonstrated terrain workflow, the platform used an SRTM elevation raster, generated an implementation plan, handled projected units, and produced slope and aspect rasters for inspection.

01

Slope

Generate slope from elevation data.

02

Aspect

Generate downslope direction from elevation data.

03

Hillshade

Visualize terrain relief using the supported terrain toolset.

04

Depression filling

Prepare an elevation surface for terrain and hydrology processing.

Units and undefined values matter.

The demonstrated slope/aspect workflow used projected, meter-based coordinates. Aspect on flat cells was treated as NoData, preserving an undefined direction rather than inventing one.

05 / HYDROLOGY ANALYSIS

Model flow and drainage from elevation data

GriidAi includes Whitebox-based terrain and hydrology tools for depression filling, flow direction, flow accumulation, stream extraction, watershed delineation, and subbasin generation, with related terrain derivatives available in the same environment.

  1. 01

    Prepare the DEM

    Fill depressions where appropriate to the analysis.

  2. 02

    Model flow direction

    Calculate the direction of modeled surface flow from elevation.

  3. 03

    Accumulate flow

    Examine where modeled flow concentrates across the terrain.

  4. 04

    Extract drainage

    Derive stream networks and examine watershed or subbasin outputs.

Multiple tables can be opened in the table drawer, with selections remaining visible in the map context.

08 / MULTI-STEP ANALYSIS

Chain operations into a larger analytical sequence

Many useful spatial questions require more than one GIS operation. GriidAi connects supported GIS primitives into multi-step analysis. Demonstrations show a sequence from inspection to masking, terrain derivation, raster calculation, building-level summarization, and classification within one analysis session.

ROOFTOP SOLAR SCREENING EXAMPLE
  1. 01

    Audit

    Inspect building footprints and surface data; check CRS, resolution, and overlap.

  2. 02

    Mask

    Use building zones to retain relevant raster cells while preserving the source grid.

  3. 03

    Derive

    Calculate terrain/surface derivatives needed by the screening method.

  4. 04

    Model

    Calculate incident solar-energy screening values under stated assumptions.

  5. 05

    Summarize

    Aggregate raster results to each building and write values to attributes.

  6. 06

    Validate

    Run sanity checks and inspect the resulting map/table before interpretation.

09 / ANALYTICAL CONTEXT

Spatial analysis depends on more than choosing the right tool

A correct-looking map can still be analytically wrong if coordinate systems, units, raster alignment, NoData values, or field meanings are mishandled. Keep this context visible as you review the method and interpret the result.

CRS & projection

Check the spatial reference and units used by the method.

Raster resolution

Inspect pixel size and alignment when they affect the analysis.

NoData

Preserve undefined or missing raster values.

Metadata

Inspect structural and spatial context alongside the data.

Area of interest

Constrain search, clipping, and analysis to the relevant area.

10 / HUMAN REVIEW & VALIDATION

Review the method before trusting the result

For supported tasks, GriidAi presents an implementation plan before execution so the user can review the selected inputs, method, validation strategy, and expected output. After processing, the analyst can inspect the resulting map, layer, table, and statistics and decide whether another iteration is needed.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Understanding AI-guided spatial analysis

Can AI perform spatial analysis?

GriidAi connects AI guidance to supported GIS operations. The spatial data, method, parameters, and outputs remain part of the review and validation process.

Can I work with both vector and raster data?

Yes. Supported workflows include vector operations such as buffer and intersection, raster calculations and zonal statistics, and analysis combining the two data families.

How do I validate the analysis?

Review the selected inputs, coordinate systems and units, method, parameters, and validation strategy. Inspect intermediate and final outputs before deciding how the result should be used.

Does GriidAi replace GIS experts or every GIS tool?

GriidAi is a guided cloud workspace for supported geospatial analysis. It keeps methodological judgment and interpretation with the expert and does not replace every GIS tool.
